content:
Apple is widely expected to launch a brand-new iPad mini with an OLED display later this month. Today, an unverified new rumour once again claims the new iPad mini will switch to an OLED display, but will still only have a 60Hz refresh rate, with no ProMotion support.

OLED iPad mini may lack ProMotion

This is the second time we have heard this rumour, but both times it has come from the same source: the yeux1122 account on Naver. This account has a mixed track record for Apple rumours, and often seems to be passing along information from anonymous sources rather than providing first-hand information.

However, yeux1122's latest post claims that although 'some overseas sources mention 120Hz', 'local production volumes have confirmed' it will use a 60Hz display.

I want to emphasise again that I am quite sceptical of this rumour, as there are no other reliable sources to corroborate it at present.

However, if true, it would be a rather disappointing limitation for iPad mini buyers. The iPad mini upgrade is expected to bring several other notable changes, including:

  • An OLED display.
  • An upgrade from the current iPad mini's A17 Pro chip to the Apple A20 Pro chip.
  • A redesigned look with narrower bezels and potentially improved water resistance.
  • The FaceTime camera will move to the landscape edge, similar to the design of Apple's other iPad models.

If Apple makes so many changes but ultimately fails to upgrade the display to ProMotion with a 120Hz refresh rate, it would significantly diminish the arrival of the new iPad mini.

The new iPad mini is expected to launch later this month, so we won't have to wait too long to find out the answer.

What do you think? Will the new iPad mini feature ProMotion and a 120Hz refresh rate? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
